You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Sotheby's (Beijing) Auction Co. joint venture, realized ~3-5-year record

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> the transaction was structured at closing; it reports only the realized post-formation
> record. The outcome window is fixed as the registrant's fiscal 2016 annual report
> (filed 2017-02-27), roughly four years after the September 2012 formation.

## Public-reporting status (feasibility of an outcome record)
- The registrant (Sotheby's, CIK 823094) continued filing annual reports on EDGAR through
  the outcome window; its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016 was filed
  on 2017-02-27, so a public realized record exists. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

## Realized ownership and consolidation status
- As of the FY2016 report, Sotheby's (Beijing) Auction Co., Ltd. ("Sotheby's Beijing") —
  the joint venture formed in September 2012 — remained a consolidated entity in which the
  registrant held a controlling 80% ownership interest; the 20% non-controlling interest
  continued to be reported within equity. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- No divestiture, put-option exercise, dissolution, or wind-up of Sotheby's Beijing is
  disclosed in the FY2016 report; the venture was retained on the same 80/20 basis through
  the window. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

## Best-documented realized scalar (venture-specific)
- Sotheby's Beijing is the registrant's only consolidated entity with a non-controlling
  interest, so the reported "Net (Loss) Income Attributable to Noncontrolling Interest"
  isolates 20% of the venture's result. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- Net (loss) income attributable to the non-controlling interest was $(73) thousand in
  2016, $(246) thousand in 2015, and $197 thousand in 2014 — a swing from a small share of
  profit in 2014 to small shares of loss in 2015 and 2016 (i.e., the venture at 100%
  implies roughly $985K income in 2014, $1.23M loss in 2015, and $365K loss in 2016).
  [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

## Realized scalar (registrant-wide, for context)
- Net income attributable to Sotheby's was $74.112 million (2016), $43.727 million (2015),
  and $117.795 million (2014); diluted EPS was $1.27, $0.63, and $1.68 respectively. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- Total revenues were $805.377 million (2016), $961.494 million (2015), and $938.053
  million (2014); the registrant stated that after the expansion of the global art market,
  fourth-quarter 2015 and full-year 2016 auction results indicated the market had "entered
  a period of lower sales." [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- Revenue attributable to "Hong Kong and China" was $145.885 million (2016), $146.262
  million (2015), and $165.066 million (2014). [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

## Documented interface conditions over time
- The registrant continued to identify the joint venture contracts (dated September 3, 2012
  and amended September 26, 2012) as material agreements in its FY2016 exhibit index,
  indicating the venture agreement remained in force through the window. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- In describing competition in the Chinese art market, the registrant named local rivals
  (Beijing Poly International Auction Co., China Guardian Auctions Co., and Beijing Hanhai
  Auction Co.) but did not report the Beijing Free Port venture as a material revenue
  contributor; no separate operating narrative for Sotheby's Beijing beyond the
  consolidation note and the non-controlling-interest line is disclosed. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]
- No impairment, write-down, or disruption specifically attributed to Sotheby's Beijing is
  disclosed in the FY2016 report. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Through the fixed outcome window (FY2016, ~four years after formation), the joint venture
  was retained and consolidated on its original 80/20 basis with no divestiture or
  impairment disclosed; its only separately identifiable financial trace — the 20%
  non-controlling-interest line — moved from a small profit share in 2014 to small loss
  shares in 2015 and 2016, while the registrant disclosed no distinct operating narrative
  for the venture. [SRC: SEC accession 0000823094-17-000009, Form 10-K for FY2016]

[SLICE END]
